indicators.note: the farm worker is said to hold the line, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a peasant is a rural labourer

explanation.surface: A countryman described as nice, gripping a rope or a line of some sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something nice is agreeable or enjoyable.

clue.text: Fight in Greek city-state? No thanks!

indicators.note: 'No thanks' tells us to drop the word for thanks from the city name

parts.note: Sparta was a city-state of ancient Greece
TA is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: An offer of a fight in ancient Sparta, politely declined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' removes TA (British slang for thanks) from SPARTA.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to spar is to box or argue, a form of fighting.

indicators.note: the word for talk is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to rabbit (on) is British slang for chatter at length

explanation.surface: A cleric who talks on and on without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' drops the T from RABBIT; 'rabbit' meaning chatter is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a rabbi is a Jewish teacher and spiritual leader.

clue.text: We bring potty for making beer

indicators.note: potty means crazy, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A brewer using a pot for beer-making.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: fermenting ale from malt and hops is the process called brewing.

clue.text: Paddle right behind middle of boat

indicators.note: the right abbreviation is placed behind, after, the middle letters
the central letters of the word boat are taken

explanation.surface: Instructions for paddling: sit on the right behind the centre of the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' boat gives OA; 'right' gives R and 'behind' puts it after OA. The clue word 'right' supplies R.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an oar is a pole with a blade used to paddle or row a boat.

clue.text: Free lunch at first I criticised strongly

indicators.note: only the opening letter of lunch is used

parts.note: to berate is to scold harshly

explanation.surface: Someone complaining loudly about a free lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: freed people have been released from captivity.

parts.note: a mode is a fashion; with the 's it gives the word plus S

indicators.note: only the first letter of trend is used

explanation.surface: A demure look as the beginning of a fashion trend.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: demure and modest both describe someone shy and unassuming.

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A cigar spoiled by mould.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: agaric is a kind of mushroom with gills.

parts.note: having a gander is British slang for having a look
following means coming after

explanation.surface: A goose trailing behind a nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gander' is the male goose on the surface, but here it means a look.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to nurse someone is to tend and care for them.

indicators.note: the word for swine loses its last letter

parts.note: a boar is a male pig

explanation.surface: A snake or a pig falling behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a boa is a large constricting snake.

definitions.meaning: a flat-bottomed drinking vessel without a stem
one who performs somersaults and falls

explanation.surface: A circus performer's choice of drinking vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a plain drinking vessel, and a gymnast who does flips.

clue.text: Availing oneself of gun is wrong

indicators.note: the letters are put in a wrong order and must be fixed

explanation.surface: A moral warning that resorting to a firearm is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' belongs to the fodder; 'wrong' rearranges GUN IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: availing oneself of something means making use of it.

indicators.note: the word for stagger is read backwards

parts.note: to stagger someone is to stun them with surprise

explanation.surface: Fanatics reeling backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: nuts informally means enthusiasts or obsessive fans.

clue.text: Recluse rings academic person at home in capital

indicators.note: the word for recluse encircles the academic

parts.note: a loner keeps to themself
a don is a university lecturer

explanation.surface: A hermit phoning a lecturer who is at home in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rings' looks like phoning but means surrounding.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a native or resident of the capital city of England.

parts.note: per means for each, as in per head
a form is a school class in Britain

explanation.surface: Staging a play for every class in a school.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to play a piece of music or a role is to perform it.

clue.text: Remnant of fire at end of three months

definitions.meaning: a glowing coal left after burning
the shared final letters of September, November and December

explanation.surface: The last of a fire glowing after a long season.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a glowing coal, and the closing letters of three month names.

clue.text: Hum and haw as foolish female slurred

indicators.note: spoken drunkenly, so the S sounds become SH sounds

parts.note: a silly Sally, Sally being a woman's name

explanation.surface: A dithering, scatterbrained woman who mumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'silly Sally' with a drunken slur and each S turns into SH.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to hum and haw is to dither indecisively, as is to shilly-shally.

clue.text: Rich man flipping an old coin

indicators.note: the little word an is turned over and read in reverse

parts.note: a bob was the British shilling before decimal currency

explanation.surface: A wealthy man tossing an old shilling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' turns 'an' to NA; BOB is an old British shilling.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a nabob is a person of great wealth, originally from India.

parts.note: a particular is a detail or point
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: The Queen walking behind a particular dog she prefers.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a pointer is a gun dog breed that indicates game.

indicators.note: the soldier breaks into the word for free, splitting it

parts.note: to rid is to free or clear
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A stubborn soldier breaking out to freedom.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: rigid means stiff and unbending.

clue.text: Like Robin's men, make a detour to see Carousel

parts.note: Robin Hood's band were the Merry Men
to go round is to take a detour

explanation.surface: Robin Hood's band detouring to watch the musical Carousel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carousel' looks like the Rodgers and Hammerstein musical but is a fairground ride.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a carousel is a revolving fairground ride with horses.

clue.text: Short commissionaire has time for put-upon person

indicators.note: the word for commissionaire is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a uniformed doorman at a hotel or office

explanation.surface: A doorman whose shift is short of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' drops N from DOORMAN; a commissionaire is a uniformed attendant at a British hotel or cinema door.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a person walked over by others, like the mat people wipe their feet on.

definitions.meaning: a warhorse ridden by a knight

explanation.surface: Asking whether the horse wants paying.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: one who bills for a service, and a cavalry mount.

parts.note: Eton is a famous English public school

explanation.surface: A pupil confessing to having left school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' is a verb on the surface but gives L. ETON is an elite English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to let on is to reveal or confess something.

indicators.note: the letters are packed away inside the phrase

explanation.surface: A trunk somehow packed into a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunk' suggests luggage, but it is the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the trunk of a body, without head and limbs.

clue.text: Child starts to behave and is rarely naughty

indicators.note: the opening letter of each of these words is taken

explanation.surface: A child who behaves and is seldom naughty.
explanation.walkthrough: BAIRN is the Scottish word for child.
explanation.definitionFit: Regional synonym: in Scotland and northern England a child is a bairn.
